examples.text: Our children attend a public school in our neighborhood.

glosses: An educational institution providing primary and secondary education, prior to tertiary education (college or university).

examples.text: One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on schools[…]as children, teachers or school buildings become the targets of attacks. examples.text: Divinity, history and geography are studied for two schools per week.

glosses: Within a larger educational institution, an organizational unit, such as a department or institute, which is dedicated to a specific subject area.

examples.text: We are enrolled in the same university, but I attend the School of Economics and my brother is in the School of Music.

examples.text: The Barbizon school of painters were part of an art movement towards Realism in art, which arose in the context of the dominant Romantic movement of the time.

examples.text: These economists belong to the monetarist school.

glosses: The time during which classes are attended or in session in an educational institution.

examples.text: I’ll see you after school.

glosses: The room or hall in English universities where the examinations for degrees and honours are held.

glosses: Établissement d'enseignement préparant les élèves à des emplois techniques ou de bureau.

examples.text: Les annonces classées des grands quotidiens se remplissent alors de nombreuses pages d'annonces pour différentes écoles professionnelles, privés ou publiques : les business colleges constituent souvent 40 % de toutes ces publicités.

En 1868, Jules Simon publie un article d’une page dans l’Illustration sur les écoles professionnelles de jeunes filles. Connu pour ses analyses sur le travail et le salaire des femmes ainsi que pour son opposition au travail des femmes en « atelier », il préconise ici le développement d’écoles professionnelles qui permettent aux femmes de travailler dans la maison : « les professions de comptables, de lingères, de peintres, de graveuses, peuvent s’exercer dans la maison […] c’est précisément ce que les fondatrices ont voulu ».
